messages.text:
You are a research and data subagent for the research agent "claude", which is building an in-house 3D MHD solar-wind model (coronal model at 0.1 AU feeding a heliospheric MHD code, similar in spirit to WSA-ENLIL or EUHFORIA). The goal is to estimate the solar-wind flux at interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS during its XMM-Newton observation, 2025-12-03T12:04 to 2025-12-04T10:12 UTC. The comet was at about 1.88 AU, about 70° east of Earth in heliocentric longitude and about 25° east of STEREO-A, near the ecliptic. Plasma reaching the comet then left the Sun around 2025-11-20 to 2025-11-30. Work fully autonomously: no human will answer questions.

WORKSPACE (write only here): /mnt/c/Users/cabot/OneDrive/Documents/Research/Cambridge/X3I/mhd_llm/claude/data/ (subfolders gong/, adapt/, hmi/, cme/, ips/, wsa_ccmc/, qc/; scripts in data/scripts_rs/). Never write to mhd_llm/argon, mhd_llm/codex, or mhd_llm/shared_notes. Reference: the CCMC ENLIL run the reviewer recommended is mirrored at mhd_llm/claude/ref/ccmc/ (control file; CME cone list Jan_Deca_120925_SH_1_cme_param.txt from DONKI with v≥600 km/s and width≥30°; boundary list Jan_Deca_120925_SH_1_wsadu_gongz.lst naming hourly WSA v5.4 GONGz maps, e.g. /wsadw_5.4/gongz/2025/11/wsadw_gongz_20251125T0014.fits). The preprint text is at mhd_llm/claude/ref/main.txt.

RESOURCES: shared machine. Use at most 4 CPU threads, at most 3 GB RAM, and no GPU. Total download under about 3 GB. Wrap heavy Python in `systemd-run --user --scope --quiet -p MemoryMax=3G ...`. Python: /home/scabot/miniconda3/bin/python3 (numpy, scipy, astropy, matplotlib, pandas). /home/scabot/miniconda3/envs/mhd_claude/bin/python (adds sunpy, h5py) is being built now; use it if present. Parse downloaded files with `python -I`. CODE STYLE (user mandate): minimal, with no comments and no docstrings, and no "note" fields in output JSON. Caveats go in the README. American spelling.

TASKS
1. Research memo, data/remote_sensing_memo.md (concise, with citations and URLs). Which remote-sensing products of the Sun and the solar wind matter to LEADING ORDER for the ion flux at a point near 1.9 AU over a ~1-day window, and how should each enter a WSA+MHD model? Cover:
   - photospheric synoptic magnetograms: GONG mrzqs (zero-point-corrected, daily-updated synoptic), ADAPT-GONG (flux-transport ensemble, 12 realizations), SDO/HMI synoptic and daily-updated maps; Solar Orbiter PHI far-side maps, if any, for the Nov 2025 far side. Note that the comet's sub-solar longitude region was partly on the far side as seen from Earth: quantify how old the magnetogram data are at the Carrington longitudes that map to the comet;
   - coronal-hole EUV maps (SDO/AIA 193, STEREO-A/EUVI) as a WSA check;
   - CME catalogs (DONKI CMEAnalysis, CACTus, SOHO/LASCO CDAW), giving cone-model parameters for CMEs directed toward the comet's longitude between Nov 15 and Dec 4 2025;
   - interplanetary scintillation (ISEE/Nagoya IPS velocity maps; LOFAR), heliospheric imagers (STEREO-A/HI, PUNCH), and white-light coronagraphs used for density/streamer constraints;
   - in-situ data assimilation (BRaVDA; Lang & Owens), WSA coefficient calibrations (Arge et al. 2003/2004; McGregor et al. 2011; Riley et al. 2015; Reiss et al. 2019/2020), and the ENLIL/EUHFORIA inner-boundary prescriptions (Odstrcil 2003; Pomoell & Poedts 2018). Give the exact WSA velocity formula and coefficients used by WSA v5.x / ENLIL a6b1, and the density/temperature/Br prescriptions used by ENLIL and by EUHFORIA.
   Rank the inputs by their expected influence on the comet-site flux.
2. Downloads:
   a) GONG mrzqs daily-updated synoptic maps: one per day (closest to 00 UT), 2025-10-15 to 2025-12-06, from https://gong.nso.edu/data/magmap/ (the QR synoptic zero-corrected product, mrzqs; inspect the directory layout first). Save to data/gong/ and write data/gong/index.csv (file, map_time_utc, carrington_rotation, cr_lon_at_map_time if in the header).
   b) ADAPT-GONG maps (https://gong.nso.edu/adapt/maps/): one file per day for the same dates, if available. These are 12-realization FITS. Save to data/adapt/ with an index.
   c) HMI synoptic maps for CR 2302–2305 (JSOC hmi.Synoptic_Mr_720s or the small-format versions) as a cross-check, if downloadable without an account (otherwise skip and say so).
   d) The CCMC WSA output maps named in the boundary list: try to locate public copies on the CCMC web server (try paths like https://ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/RoR_WWW/SH/ENLIL/2025/Jan_Deca_120925_SH_1/..., the "run_files.php?runnumber=Jan_Deca_120925_SH_1" listing, or the iSWA WSA archive at https://iswa.gsfc.nasa.gov/ or https://iswaa-webservice1.ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/). If found, download about one per day for Nov 15–Dec 4 2025 into data/wsa_ccmc/ and document the FITS layout (which HDUs or planes hold v, Br, and so on). The CCMC server often returns transient "500 Proxy Error / SSL handshake" pages. Retry with backoff, and check file sizes or contents, since error pages come back as small HTML files.
   e) DONKI CME analyses (most-accurate flag) for 2025-11-01 to 2025-12-06 (try https://kauai.ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/DONKI/WS/get/CMEAnalysis?startDate=...&endDate=...&mostAccurateOnly=true, and the NASA API https://api.nasa.gov/DONKI/CMEAnalysis?api_key=[REDACTED] Save as data/cme/donki_cme_analysis.json and a tidy CSV (time21_5, lat, lon (HEEQ), half_width, speed, type, note of catalog ID). Compare with the CCMC cme_param.txt list and flag any CME whose cone, after accounting for HEEQ geometry, could plausibly intersect the comet's position (r ~1.85–1.9 AU, HEEQ lon ~ +65–75° at the time; get a rough comet HEEQ track from Horizons or compute it) between Nov 28 and Dec 5. Estimate arrival times with a simple constant-speed or drag-based model.
   f) ISEE IPS velocity data for Nov–Dec 2025 (https://stsw1.isee.nagoya-u.ac.jp/), if publicly downloadable. Otherwise document availability.
3. QC PNGs in data/qc/: one GONG mrzqs map and one ADAPT realization near 2025-11-25 (Carrington lon/lat, saturated ±20 G); the CME directions vs comet HEEQ longitude versus time; data-age map (days since each Carrington longitude was last near Earth-view central meridian) at 2025-11-25.
4. data/README_remote_sensing.md: what you downloaded, formats, header keywords for map time and Carrington longitude, gaps, and caveats.

FINAL REPLY (compact): files written; the ranked list of leading-order inputs with a one-line justification each; the WSA formula and coefficients plus the ENLIL/EUHFORIA boundary prescriptions you found (with citations); whether the CCMC WSA maps are obtainable and their layout; CMEs that could hit the comet near the XMM window; and any surprises.

<system-reminder>
Your final report is delivered through SubagentHandback: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}). The call ends your run, so make it your last step. Only a SubagentHandback call reaches your caller as your result; plain text you write at the end is not delivered. Do not also send the report with SendMessage: your caller would get it twice.
</system-reminder>

Most Recent Synoptic Map Set from GONG Standard Map Janus Map Carrington Rotation: 2316_025    16 Oct 2026 21:14 UT Magnetogram Count: 5651 Last Hour Magnetogram Count: 7 Standard Magnetogram Synoptic Maps These images show near-real-time synoptic magnetograms ― full-surface maps of the photospheric magnetic flux density, measured in Gauss. Full-disk photospheric magnetograms from GONG's six sites are used to derive a map of the magnetic field over the entire surface of the Sun. This full-surface map is called a synoptic map because it provides a general view of the field condensed from many minute-by-minute images. First of all, the GONG one-minute images are used to create 10-minute averages which are in turn remapped into longitude, measured from the central meridian, and sine(latitude). These remapped images are then shifted to the appropriate longitude in the Carrington frame and merged together in a weighted sum to form a full-surface picture of the solar magnetic field. Weighting factors of the form cosine 4 (longitude) ensure that measurements taken at a particular Carrington time contribute most to that Carrington longitude in the synoptic map.
